caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001262
attempts.paper_title: Single-unit data for sensory neuroscience: Responses from the auditory nerve of young-adult and aging gerbils
attempts.entry_title: Auditory nerve fibres of young-adult and aging gerbils (Heeringa 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of the data descriptor by Heeringa (2024) on dandiset 001262, which holds 1160 single auditory nerve fibres from 104 gerbils, one NWB file per fibre. It checks the counts and animal characteristics of Table 1, the recording types per age group, the exclusion of units with short inter-spike intervals, and the physiological properties of Figures 6 and 7 (thresholds and spontaneous rates across best frequency, phase locking, characteristic frequency and click latency, the last three recomputed from the spike times with the paper's functions).

outcomes.statement: The dataset holds 104 experiments (gerbils) with 1160 single auditory nerve fibres; 60 young-adult (32 female), 13 middle-aged (7 female) and 31 old (11 female) gerbils, with 759, 87 and 314 single units.
outcomes.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2; Table 1
outcomes.quote: The dataset consists of 104 experiments, with a total of 1160 single auditory nerve fibres ... Number of animals (number of females) 60 (32) 13 (7) 31 (11) ... Total number of single units 759 87 314
outcomes.notes: All eleven counts match. Animals are counted by subject_id (each subject's metadata is the same in all its files), age groups by age in days as the paper's code defines them.

outcomes.statement: Mean ages of the groups are 5.5, 22.5 and 38.3 months, mean ABR thresholds 18.1, 34.2 and 49.0 dB SPL, and mean weights 74.6, 83.4 and 86.4 g (young adult, middle aged, old).
outcomes.source: Table 1
outcomes.notes: All nine means are within tolerance and equal Table 1 when rounded to one decimal (5.547, 83.354 and the others printed to three decimals); the SDs and ranges also match (ABR SD 5.33, 10.19 and 18.00). 10 young adults and 1 middle-aged animal have NaN for the ABR threshold and are left out, as the code's omitnan does. The ABR means rest on reading the stored character as its code point.
deviations: The ABR threshold is not readable as written; general/notes ends with one character, or NaN. It is read as the character's code point (for example '#' is 35), an interpretation the data support (all values are multiples of 5 from 10 to 85 dB SPL, the range of Table 1, and the group means and SDs then equal Table 1's) but do not prove.

outcomes.statement: Best frequencies range from 428 to 15,825 Hz in young adults, 350 to 15,091 Hz in middle-aged and 620 to 15,762 Hz in old gerbils.
outcomes.source: Table 1
outcomes.quote: Range of best frequency in Hz 428–15,825 350–15,091 620–15,762
outcomes.notes: 428 to 15,825 Hz, 350 to 15,091 Hz and 620 to 15,762 Hz, the paper's values exactly. 8 units have no BF recording; 5 of them have a CF recording, and their recomputed CFs (700 to 4000 Hz) lie inside the young-adult range, so the ranges are the same with or without them.
deviations: The CF of units without a BF recording is recomputed (see fig7a-cf-matches-bf); it does not change any bound.

outcomes.statement: ABR thresholds rise with age, and hearing loss varies widely among the old animals.
outcomes.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2; Figure 3; Table 1
outcomes.quote: a rough estimate of hearing sensitivity, as determined by the auditory brainstem response (ABR) to chirps (0.3–19 kHz), is plotted as a function of the animal’s age (Fig. 3 ). Note the large variability in age-related hearing loss among the old animals
outcomes.notes: Mean ABR threshold 18.1, 34.2 and 49.0 dB SPL from young to old; the old animals' SD (18.0) is the largest (5.3 and 10.2 in the others), with old thresholds from 20 to 85 dB SPL. Over 93 animals age and threshold correlate (Spearman rho 0.85, p = 5.7e-27).
deviations: The ABR threshold is not readable as written; general/notes ends with one character, or NaN. It is read as the character's code point (for example '#' is 35), an interpretation the data support (all values are multiples of 5 from 10 to 85 dB SPL, the range of Table 1, and the group means and SDs then equal Table 1's) but do not prove.

outcomes.statement: Old gerbils are skewed towards males (11 of 31 female), which the paper attributes to ovarian cancer and early death of old females.
outcomes.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Note the slightly skewed distribution of quiet-aged gerbils towards more males
outcomes.notes: 11 of 31 old animals are female (0.355), against 32 of 60 young adults (0.533). Fisher's exact test, which the paper does not report, gives p = 0.125. The cause is not tested.

outcomes.statement: Of the 104 gerbils, 78 received additional oxygen throughout the experiment.
outcomes.source: Methods, Surgical procedures, Anaesthesia, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Of the total of 104 gerbils, 78 received additional oxygen (flow 1.5 l/min) in front of the tracheotomy or snout throughout the experiment
outcomes.notes: 78 of 104 animals have 'oxygen yes' in general/surgery (41 young, 6 middle aged, 31 old).

outcomes.statement: Responses to paired noise bursts were recorded in 21 of 104 experiments, Schroeder-phase stimuli in 5, and consonant-vowel-consonant logatomes in 17.
outcomes.source: Methods, Data acquisition, Complex acoustic stimuli, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: in 21 of 104 experiments, responses to two 1-s noise bursts were recorded ... in 5 of 104 experiments, responses to Schroeder-phase harmonic tone complexes ... In 17 of 104 experiments, responses to consonant-vowel-consonant logatomes were recorded
outcomes.notes: NOISE in 21, SPS in 5 and CVC in 17 of 104 experiments (143, 22 and 135 units).

outcomes.statement: CF recordings were obtained for 119 fibres, CLICK for 261, SR for 203, NOISE for 143, SPS for 22 and CVC for 135.
outcomes.source: Figure 7 legend
outcomes.quote: For fibres for which a CF recording was obtained (n = 119) ... For fibres for which a CLICK recording was obtained (n = 261) ... For fibres for which a SR recording was obtained (n = 203) ... NOISE (n = 143, panel d ), SPS (n = 22, panel e ), and CVC (n = 135, panel f )
outcomes.notes: Five of six counts match under both readings (CF 119, SR 203, NOISE 143, SPS 22, CVC 135). CLICK does not; 275 units have one CLICK recording each, and 271 give a recomputed 2-bin latency (272 with a 5 ms click delay), against 261. The files hold no stored latency, so it cannot be told which 10 units had none in the paper, or whether some had a second CLICK recording in the MATLAB files that the code would leave out. 1 CLICK unit has 75 spikes or fewer. The mismatch does not rest on the assumed click delay; reading 2 (275) uses no latency, and reading 1 gives 270 to 272 units for delays from 5 to 8.25 ms. The delay checks are consistent with 7.75 ms. The population PSTH of the CLICK trials is flat up to 8.25 ms and rises from 8.25 ms in the 20 ms trials and from 8.75 ms in the 10 ms trials, whose units have lower BFs (median 2060 against 5570 Hz). Latencies of the 10 ms trials lie on the same latency-BF line as those of the 20 ms trials (median residual -0.032 against -0.027 ms) and span 0.71 to 1.84 ms. click_polarity is 'COND' in every CLICK trial. No 500-trial recording shows signs of two joined recordings (halves differ in latency by a median 0.026 ms, odd against even trials 0.020 ms).
deviations: The stored CF and click latency are not in the files; reading 1 uses the values recomputed with the paper's functions.

The click delay is not in the files (the trial table gives NaN for CLICK trials). The 2-bin latency of Clickextract_func.m and getFSL2bins.m needs it; 7.75 ms, the delay of every tone recording in the dataset, is assumed, and 5 ms is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: No SR, SPS or CVC recordings were obtained in middle-aged gerbils, and SPS responses were recorded only in young adults.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7c to 7f
outcomes.quote: No SR, SPS, and CVC recordings were obtained in middle-aged gerbils, while SPS responses were only recorded in young-adult gerbils
outcomes.notes: No middle-aged unit has an SR, SPS or CVC recording; all 22 SPS units are from young adults.

outcomes.statement: Units with multiple inter-spike intervals below 0.6 ms, the absolute refractoriness of auditory nerve fibres, were excluded from the dataset.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 1; Figure 4b
outcomes.quote: Units with multiple inter-spike intervals <0.6 ms, which is the absolute refractoriness of auditory nerve fibres ... were excluded from the dataset
outcomes.notes: Units with two or more within-trial ISIs below 0.6 ms are in the dataset under every reading, 370 of 1160 under (a), 391 under (b), 148 under (c), from 79 of 104 animals; 538 units have at least one. In failing units short ISIs are a median 0.13% of all ISIs (largest 22.3%), and 162 units have more than 10. Of 13,904 short ISIs, 10,192 are 0.3 to 0.6 ms and 1171 below 0.1 ms. With a 0.3 ms limit 140 units fail under (a), with 0.1 ms 5 do. Spike times are sorted within trials and no spike train is duplicated. The paper's check was visual (checkAN.m plots the count); it does not say how many short ISIs 'multiple' allows. Many short ISIs appear to be double detections of one spike. In the voltage trace, all ISIs below 0.1 ms (from 9 units), 91% of those from 0.1 to 0.3 ms and 39% of those from 0.3 to 0.6 ms lie on one waveform (the trace does not fall below half the smaller peak between the two spike times), against none of 300 pairs from 0.8 to 1.5 ms. Below 0.1 ms (median dip ratio 0.95) this shows a double detection; the rule was not checked at 0.3 to 0.6 ms, so there it is a plausible reading, not a demonstration. The outcome stands, since the paper's check counts ISIs from the same spike times; counting only pairs that are not one waveform, 176 units still fail under (a) and 179 under (b).
deviations: A recording is taken as a recording type of the unit; each type occurs once per unit in the files.

outcomes.statement: No median spike waveform showed a prepotential, which would mark a ventral cochlear nucleus bushy cell.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, first criterion; Figure 4d
outcomes.quote: We did not encounter any prepotentials in our recordings
outcomes.notes: The check was a visual inspection of the median spike waveform (checkAN.m); neither the paper nor its code gives a rule for a prepotential, so no criterion fixed from the paper can judge it, as the claims file says. The raw voltage traces are in the files (acquisition), so the waveforms are available; they were not read.

outcomes.statement: Rate-level functions were checked for atypical shapes (auditory nerve rate-level functions are typically straight, sloping saturating or flat saturating), and units whose rate-level function was nonmonotonic at levels below 80 dB SPL were excluded.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, second criterion; Figure 5a
outcomes.quote: When a rate-level function showed nonmonotonicity at levels lower than 80 dB SPL, it indicated that the spikes derived from a non-primary cell receiving inhibitory input. The unit was then excluded from the dataset
outcomes.notes: The check was visual and the paper gives no rule for nonmonotonicity. As a description only, with rates per level computed from the spike times in the stimulus window (the stored rates are not in the files), 249 of 952 RLF recordings have a fall in mean rate between successive levels below 80 dB SPL larger than the SD at the lower level, and 104 have two or more.

outcomes.statement: The example fibre of Fig. 5b (animal G220908, unit 3p_181) had a best frequency of 7.6 kHz and a threshold of 19 dB SPL.
outcomes.source: Figure 5b legend
outcomes.quote: This fibre had a best frequency of 7.6 kHz and a threshold at 19 dB SPL
outcomes.notes: Stored BF 7620 Hz and RLF threshold 19 dB SPL. The BF recording is at 30 dB SPL with 5 repetitions per frequency, and the RLF recording (7700 Hz) has 10 repetitions per level and includes 40 dB SPL, as the legend says.

outcomes.statement: Fibres of young-adult gerbils show two regions of best sensitivity separated by a region around 3 to 4 kHz with higher thresholds and fewer fibres; the highest thresholds are at 3.5 kHz.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 6a
outcomes.quote: Fibres of young-adult gerbils exhibited two regions of best sensitivity (lowest thresholds), separated by a frequency region (around 3–4 kHz) with slightly less sensitive and fewer fibres ... For the young-adult gerbils in the current dataset, highest thresholds were at 3.5 kHz
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b) the highest young-adult mean threshold between the two sensitive regions is 27.6 dB SPL in the bin plotted at 3.48 kHz, with 25.4 and 24.4 dB in the neighbouring bins; the sensitive regions have their lowest means at 1.73 kHz (20.9 dB) and 8.34 kHz (21.2 dB), which are also the two lowest bin means of all bins. Under reading (a) the highest mean of all bins is 36.7 dB at 0.72 kHz, from 3 units. The criterion is met under one reading, as it requires. The bins plotted at 2.06 to 4.14 kHz hold 30 to 34 units, fewer than at 4.93 to 11.83 kHz (43 to 83) and about as many as at 1.02 to 1.73 kHz (33 to 36).
deviations: The two readings of 'highest' differ; the claims file's criterion takes the claim as reproduced under either, and only (b) holds.

outcomes.statement: Among young-adult fibres, the fewest best frequencies fall in the bin bordered by 2.5 and 3.0 kHz.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 2; Figure 6b
outcomes.quote: fewest fibres were in the bin bordered by 2.5 and 3.0 kHz (Fig. 6b )
outcomes.notes: The bin from 2423 to 2936 Hz holds 34 young-adult units. It is not the fewest of the non-empty span (the 356 Hz bin holds 1, and the bins below 766 Hz hold 1 to 11), nor fewer than both neighbours (34 and 35). Among the bins from 1363 to 4309 Hz it ties for the fewest (34) with the 1363 and 2000 Hz bins. With the CF of young units without a BF recording added, the bin still holds 34. In the same bins the named bin is the fewest and a local minimum only among middle-aged units (0, neighbours 6 and 5); among old units (23, neighbours 10 and 22) and all ages (57, neighbours 50 and 62) it is neither. The paper's text names young adults.

outcomes.statement: Among high-frequency fibres (BF above 3.5 kHz) there is a cluster with low spontaneous rates, and low-frequency fibres have a bimodal distribution of spontaneous rate with modes near 5 and 60 spikes/s.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 3; Figure 6c
outcomes.quote: Among the high-frequency fibres (>3.5 kHz), there was a cluster of fibres with low spontaneous rates ... The low-frequency fibres show a bimodal distribution of spontaneous rate, with a mode around 5 spikes/s and one around 60 spikes/s
outcomes.notes: Measured values are bin centres. Low-BF young-adult units (314) have their two largest modes of spontaneous rate in the bins 0 to 5 (27 units) and 55 to 60 spikes/s (21), separated by a bin of 5. A mode is a local maximum as the criterion defines it; the last bin is not one. High-BF units (437) have their largest local maximum at 0 to 5 spikes/s (66), below 18. 26.1% of high-BF and 18.5% of low-BF units are below 18 spikes/s.

outcomes.statement: The highest best frequency at which significant phase locking was recorded in young-adult gerbils was 4.6 kHz.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 4; Figure 6d
outcomes.quote: The maximum best frequency at which significant phase locking was recorded in young-adult gerbils was 4.6 kHz
outcomes.notes: The highest BF of a young-adult unit with significant phase locking (p < 0.001) is 4598 Hz; the next are 4121 to 4377 Hz. No young PH unit with a higher BF (27 units, 4718 to 12,359 Hz) reaches p < 0.001. The value depends on the threshold, 6539 Hz with p < 0.01 and 4377 Hz with p < 0.0001; the Methods fix 0.001. One PH level (a middle-aged unit) has exactly 50 spikes, the only case where the Methods' and the code's rules for a NaN p-value differ; no unit's maximum significant vector strength changes between them.
deviations: Vector strength and its p-value are not in the NWB files. They are recomputed per level of the PH recording with PHextract_func.m and TytoView_calcVS.m (Methods, 'The analysis procedures were carried out by the function PHextract_func.m'), spikes between tone onset and offset, p = exp(-N vs^2), NaN when N < 50 as the Methods say ('When N < 50, the p-value is NaN'); the code's rule (ntot > 50, NaN when N is 50 or fewer) is shown as a variant. The silent trials' value, which the code also stores, is left out.

outcomes.statement: The highest vector strengths are found among fibres with low best frequencies (below 1.5 kHz) and low spontaneous rates (below 18 spikes/s).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 4; Figure 6d
outcomes.quote: the highest vector strength values were found among the fibres with low best frequencies (<1.5 kHz) and low spontaneous rates (<18 spikes/s, shown in open markers Fig. 6d )
outcomes.notes: All four readings hold. The largest maximum vector strength (0.882) is from a unit with BF 428 Hz and SR 1.25 spikes/s, and the median is highest in the low-BF low-SR group (0.821 over 6 young adults, 0.804 over 19 units of all ages; low-BF high-SR 0.695 and 0.702). Young adults with BF below 1.5 kHz, low-SR against high-SR, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0039 (6 and 51 units).
deviations: Vector strength and its p-value are not in the NWB files. They are recomputed per level of the PH recording with PHextract_func.m and TytoView_calcVS.m (Methods, 'The analysis procedures were carried out by the function PHextract_func.m'), spikes between tone onset and offset, p = exp(-N vs^2), NaN when N < 50 as the Methods say ('When N < 50, the p-value is NaN'); the code's rule (ntot > 50, NaN when N is 50 or fewer) is shown as a variant. The silent trials' value, which the code also stores, is left out.

outcomes.statement: Characteristic frequency from the CF recordings correlates strongly with best frequency from the BF recordings, with no systematic deviation towards higher or lower frequencies.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7a
outcomes.quote: these figures confirm that the characteristic frequency derived from the CF recordings correlated strongly with the best frequency derived from the BF recordings, with no systematic deviation towards higher or lower frequencies (Fig. 7a )
outcomes.notes: Over 114 units with a recomputed CF and a stored BF, Pearson r(log CF, log BF) = 0.973 (p = 2.1e-73), Spearman 0.964; median CF/BF 1.003 (log2 0.0041, 95% bootstrap interval -0.0111 to 0.0398); 58 units above and 56 below; 13 differ by more than half an octave. Taking the levels from the calibrated level column instead of the nominal attenuator level in the tag gives the same CF for all 119 units.
deviations: The stored CF is not in the NWB files. CF is recomputed from the CF recording's spike times with CFextract_func.m, getSpikeCounts.m and getQ10dB.m (named in the Methods, 'The analysis procedures were carried out by the function CFextract_func.m'), automatic first pass only. The code asks the experimenter to accept or change the response criterion and the CF ('T could be manually adjusted when needed', Methods); those manual choices are not in the files.

outcomes.statement: Click latency is strongly negatively correlated with best frequency, reflecting the travelling wave delay along the cochlea.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7b
outcomes.quote: Click latency had a strong negative correlation to best frequency, illustrating the travelling wave delay along the cochlea (Fig. 7b )
outcomes.notes: Over 268 units, Pearson r(latency, log BF) = -0.882 (p = 5.9e-89), Spearman -0.864; negative in each age group (-0.78 to -0.92). Latencies span 0.42 to 2.78 ms; this range does not single out 7.75 ms. With a 5 ms click delay, r = -0.662 and Spearman -0.820 over 269 units, so the outcome is the same under both delays. The 10 ms and 20 ms trials give latencies on the same latency-BF line under the assumed delay, so they share one delay (recording-type-counts); the absolute delay is not established.
deviations: The stored 2-bin latency is not in the files; it is recomputed with Clickextract_func.m and getFSL2bins.m (named in the Methods).

The click delay is not in the files (the trial table gives NaN for CLICK trials). The 2-bin latency of Clickextract_func.m and getFSL2bins.m needs it; 7.75 ms, the delay of every tone recording in the dataset, is assumed, and 5 ms is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The best-frequency distributions of the units with CF and with CLICK recordings are representative of the distribution of the full dataset.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7a and 7b
outcomes.quote: BF distributions of two large datasets, CF and CLICK (Fig. 7a,b , respectively), are representative of the distribution of the full dataset (Fig. 6b )
outcomes.notes: No reading holds for both subsets. The CF units' BFs differ from both references (KS p = 0.018 against young adults, 0.003 against all units; median 3454 Hz, 0.75 times the references' 4589 and 4592 Hz). The CLICK units' BFs do not differ by KS (p = 0.20 and 0.45) but their median (5180 Hz) is 1.13 times the references'. The criterion says not reproduced 'when none does'; this record reads 'a reading holds' as holding for both CF and CLICK, as the criterion's reproduced case does. Under the other reading of 'none' (no reading holds for either subset) the claim would be blocked as methods_underspecified, since the CLICK KS reading holds.
deviations: The claims file's criterion can be read two ways when the CF and CLICK subsets give different results; the reading taken is stated in the notes.

outcomes.statement: Successful single-fibre recordings were obtained in 43% of old gerbils that were tried, against 88% of young adults.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: successful recordings of single auditory-nerve fibres were obtained in only 43% of the experimental old gerbils (compared to 88% in young adults)
outcomes.notes: The denominators are the animals operated on, including those that gave no single units. Every one of the 104 subjects has at least one unit file, and neither the files, the dandiset metadata nor its description list animals that gave none. The paper names no other deposit of them.

outcomes.statement: Responses to tones at 20 and 30 dB above threshold were examined for non-primary-like shapes, using BF, RLF and PH recordings combined when available, and units with clearly non-primary-like responses were excluded.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, third criterion; Figure 5b
outcomes.quote: The responses to tones at 20 and 30 dB above threshold were examined for non-primary-like shapes. When the response was clearly non-primary like, the unit was excluded from the dataset
outcomes.notes: The check was visual; the paper and its code (makePSTH.m) give no rule for a non-primary-like shape, as the claims file says.

findings.statement: The ABR threshold in general/notes ('threshold (db SPL) ...') is written as a single character whose code point is the threshold, for example '#' for 35 and 'K' for 75, and control characters such as a line feed for 10; 11 animals have 'NaN'. Read as code points, the values give Table 1's means and SDs exactly, so the number appears to have been converted to a character in the conversion to NWB.

The analysed outcomes the paper describes as stored with each recording (exp.data.[type].analysis) are in the NWB files only as best frequency, spontaneous rate and threshold per recording type. The characteristic frequency, Q10, vector strength with its p-value and levels, the click latencies and first-spike statistics, and the rate-level and frequency-response rates are not there. Most can be recomputed from the spike times with the paper's code, but the manual corrections the code allows (CF and response criterion, RLF threshold) cannot.

The CLICK trials carry no delay (NaN in the trial table), so the click's onset within the trial, needed for click latencies, is not in the files. The SR, NOISE, SPS and CVC trials also have no delay. The click_polarity column holds 'COND' in every CLICK trial.

Question for the paper's author. What was the click delay (curvesettings.delay) of the CLICK recordings, and was it the same in all of them? This attempt assumed 7.75 ms, the delay of every tone recording, which gives latencies of 0.42 to 2.78 ms; the correlation with best frequency is negative under 7.75 or 5 ms. The data are consistent with 7.75 ms in both the 10 ms and the 20 ms CLICK trials (the population PSTH rises from 8.25 ms, and both trial lengths give latencies on one latency-BF line), but do not fix it.

370 of 1160 units have two or more within-trial inter-spike intervals below 0.6 ms in one recording (391 pooled over recordings, 148 in the BF recording alone), although the paper says units with multiple such intervals were excluded. Most short intervals are 0.3 to 0.6 ms. About half of the 13,904 short intervals lie on one spike waveform in the voltage trace (all 1171 below 0.1 ms, 91% of those from 0.1 to 0.3 ms, 39% of those from 0.3 to 0.6 ms) by a dip-ratio rule. The intervals below 0.1 ms are double detections of single spikes; for those from 0.3 to 0.6 ms this is a plausible reading, as the rule was checked only against intervals of 0.8 to 1.5 ms. Counting only intervals between separate waveforms, 176 units still have two or more in one recording.

275 units have a CLICK recording, one each, and 271 give a 2-bin latency with the paper's function, where the Fig. 7 legend counts 261 units with a CLICK recording. Without the stored latencies the difference cannot be traced.

The recordings are extracellular single-unit recordings with a glass electrode (as the file's own device description says), but they are stored as intracellular (icephys) VoltageClampStimulusSeries, and the archive's summary lists the measurement technique as 'voltage clamp technique'.

The dataset holds only the 104 animals with recorded units. The animals operated on without a successful recording, which the paper's success rates (43% of old and 88% of young-adult gerbils) count, are not listed in the files or the metadata.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested the helper functions on synthetic data (vs_calc, short_isis, age_group, weight_g, abr_decoded, cf_from_cf_recording, click_latency_2bins) and found that they behaved as specified. It gave its own outcome for each of the 23 claims; all agree with the record. It found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. It asked for outputs on the click onset, the analysis table's columns, the CF level source, the very short ISIs and the fig6b bin counts by population. All are now printed in the notebook.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the README, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 23 outcomes and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. It found sentences the printed outputs do not support (cells 17, 37, 72 and 75, the README run time, and calling the 0.3 to 0.6 ms ISIs double detections) and asked that cell 75 name the reading of 'none does' it takes. All are corrected, and the Table 1 means are now printed to three decimals.

entries.name: 001262-heeringa-2024
entries.title: Auditory nerve fibres of young-adult and aging gerbils (Heeringa 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of the data descriptor by Heeringa (2024) on dandiset 001262, which holds 1160 single auditory nerve fibres from 104 gerbils, one NWB file per fibre. It checks the counts and animal characteristics of Table 1, the recording types per age group, the exclusion of units with short inter-spike intervals, and the physiological properties of Figures 6 and 7 (thresholds and spontaneous rates across best frequency, phase locking, characteristic frequency and click latency, the last three recomputed from the spike times with the paper's functions).
